title: Issued persona claims do not match the PersonaClaims type or the spec JSON shape
description:
The typed representation of the credential payload is dead code and the wire format has drifted from it.

persona-core/src/hvid.rs:22-35 defines PersonaClaims, documented at hvid.rs:21 as "Serialises to the exact JSON shape required by the spec", with PresenceInfo (hvid.rs:8-17) declaring:
    pub attested_at: String,    // "RFC 3339 timestamp when presence was attested"
    pub present_until: String,  // "RFC 3339 timestamp when the hardware presence attestation expires"

persona-grpc/src/service.rs:162-173 does not use either type. It hand-builds the object with serde_json::json! and emits Unix INTEGERS for both fields (service.rs:169-170, from now_secs at service.rs:156-160). Neither PersonaClaims nor PresenceInfo has any construction site outside hvid.rs and its own tests.

CONSEQUENCE: a consumer that deserialises the persona claim into persona_core::PersonaClaims - the crates own published type, which is the obvious thing to reach for - fails with a type error on attested_at and present_until. The type, its doc comment, and its round-trip test (hvid.rs:41-59) all assert a contract the daemon does not honour, so the tests give no protection against further drift.

The ponytail comment at service.rs:155 ("timestamps as Unix seconds | upgrade to RFC 3339 strings when chrono added") records the choice, but the divergence from the typed struct and from the documented spec shape is not recorded anywhere, and the test suite actively misrepresents it.

Fix direction: pick one representation and make both sides agree - either change PresenceInfo to u64 and update the doc comments and SPEC-HIA, or emit RFC 3339. Either way, build the claim by serialising PersonaClaims in service.rs rather than by hand, so the type is the single definition of the wire format.
close_reason: Duplicate of persona-5s4b.51 (same defect, filed by a second review agent from a different angle). Merged during review triage; reopen if the angle in this issue is not covered there.
